evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py:47-51 docstring: 'This includes a non-https jira.url rejection (InsecureUrlError...): detection is best-effort so the wizard stays usable to FIX a bad url'

ABSENCE: search for 'http://' in tests/unit/test_jira_onboard.py returns no matches; the two new tests (write_rejects / wizard_surfaces) pass --url http://insecure directly and never place a cleartext url in a pre-existing file that _detect() reads
advisory.finding: The _detect() fail-soft path for a cleartext jira.url is untested: no test runs the wizard (or _detect()) with a pre-existing non-https jira.url on disk to verify detection degrades gracefully instead of crashing. The change deliberately relies on InsecureUrlError being a ConfigError subclass so `except ConfigError` in _detect() swallows it (src/rebar/_cli/_jira_onboard.py:47-59), keeping the wizard usable to FIX a bad url — but a regression that narrows that except, or that stops InsecureUrlError subclassing ConfigError, would make the wizard crash on startup for anyone with a cleartext url, and no test would catch it.
scenarios: An operator already has a cleartext jira.url in rebar.toml and runs `rebar jira-onboard` to correct it; a regression narrowing _detect()'s except would abort the wizard instead of showing the bad url as the editable default.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test writing `[jira]\nurl = 'http://insecure'` to rebar.toml, then invoke main(["jira-onboard", "--project", "P", "--no-validate"]) (or call _detect() directly) and assert exit 0 with the cleartext url shown as the detected/default value — proving _detect()'s InsecureUrlError-as-ConfigError fail-soft path is exercised.

evidence: acli_subprocess.py:102-105: `except ConfigError:` then `url = os.environ.get("JIRA_URL", "")` with no _validate_https_url call on the env value
The new guard only re-raises InsecureUrlError (line 97-101); a *malformed* config takes the `except ConfigError` branch, which bypasses scheme validation entirely for the env-supplied JIRA_URL

Sink confirmed: settings.url flows to backend.py:197 `("JIRA_URL", settings.url)` and probe.py:68 `jira_url, user, token = settings.url, settings.user, settings.api_token` — handed to the credential-carrying ACLI subprocess client
JIRA_URL is the documented canonical Cloud env override (_config_sources.py:257 `("jira", "url"): "JIRA_URL"`) so `JIRA_URL=http://...` is a realistic operator value

Change goal per commit message: 'Require https for Cloud jira.url ... This risks exposing the API token / basic-auth credentials in transit' — the env-fallback path defeats this for a malformed-config scenario
test_malformed_config_falls_back_to_env (test_config_jira_wiring.py:141-148) exercises the fallback with an https env value, so the cleartext-in-fallback case is untested
advisory.finding: resolve_jira_settings' env-only fallback branch reads JIRA_URL directly from the environment with NO https-scheme validation, so a cleartext http:// URL (carrying JIRA_API_TOKEN / basic-auth to the ACLI transport) is used unvalidated whenever load_config() raises a malformed-config ConfigError — a bypass of this change's stated 'require https for Cloud jira.url' guard.
scenarios: An operator has a malformed rebar.toml (a parse error) AND exports JIRA_URL=http://jira.internal; the reconcile pass degrades to env-only and connects over cleartext, exposing the JIRA_API_TOKEN in transit — exactly the risk the change targets.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the `except ConfigError` branch, after reading `url = os.environ.get("JIRA_URL", "")`, call `_validate_https_url(url, allow_insecure=<REBAR_JIRA_ALLOW_INSECURE truthy>, url_label="JIRA_URL", override_label="jira.allow_insecure")` before returning JiraSettings.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the non-https `jira.url` rejection is an intended, documented breaking config change (migration via `jira.allow_insecure`) given it propagates through every `load_config()` consumer — including Jira-unrelated commands and the DC path that never uses `jira.url`.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_schema.py:487-496 — `def __post_init__` calls `_validate_https_url(self.url, self.allow_insecure, url_label="jira.url", ...)`, raising `InsecureUrlError` on any non-https url unless `allow_insecure`.

src/rebar/config.py:365-410 — `load_config()` returns the whole typed `Config`; `_resolve` builds every section dataclass, so `JiraConfig.__post_init__` runs on every resolve regardless of which section the caller reads.

Unrelated `load_config()` consumers that would now raise for a non-https jira.url: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:414 `load_config().mcp`, src/rebar/_cli/_audit_commands.py:145 `load_config().ui.enabled`, src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:235 `load_config().ensure`, src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py:69 `load_config().reconciler`.

src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:98-101 — the DC resolver calls `load_config()` (no `except ConfigError`) and only reads `config.reconciler`/`jira.project`, yet a non-https `jira.url` now raises `InsecureUrlError` out of it even though the DC transport connects via `reconciler.base_url`, not `jira.url` (narrowed accepted input for the DC path). Confirmed intended by tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config_jira_wiring.py:186-201.

ABSENCE: grep of the repo (tests + fixtures) shows no in-tree config sets `[jira].url` to a cleartext http:// value — the live DC harness at tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:131-141 sets only `[jira] project`, leaving `jira.url` empty so `__post_init__` skips validation. So the break bites only EXTERNAL operator configs, not any in-repo callsite.
advisory.finding: Config backward-compat tightening: `JiraConfig.__post_init__` rejects a previously-accepted non-https `[jira].url`, and because `load_config()` eagerly builds the full typed Config, the `InsecureUrlError` now propagates from EVERY `load_config()` consumer — including operations that never touch Jira (MCP server, `rebar` audit/UI gate, ensures, advisory lock, and the DC resolver which only reads `reconciler`/`jira.project`). An external operator config that legally carried a cleartext `jira.url` before this change will now fail-loud on unrelated commands.
scenarios: An operator with an existing `rebar.toml` carrying `[jira] url = "http://internal-jira"` upgrades; a subsequent `rebar` command that only reads `mcp`/`ui`/`ensure`/`reconciler` now aborts with InsecureUrlError instead of succeeding.
A Data Center deployment (which connects via reconciler.base_url) that happens to have a non-https jira.url now fails config load on the DC reconcile path.
